subject: Discovery recap — model recommendations, bench links & pilot next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carmen Diaz <carmen@orion-analytics.com>, Alex Geller <alex@orion-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Nov 2028 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap — model recommendations, bench links & pilot next steps

Hi Carmen / Alex —

Thanks again for the conversation this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we’re all aligned:

What we heard
- Primary use: multi-turn summarization + Q&A over technical docs (avg doc length ~25k tokens).
- SLAs: p50 latency <= 300ms, p95 <= 1.2s for 2k token responses in pilot; cost sensitivity at scale.
- Success metrics: accuracy on our canonical test set (we discussed the 800-case prompt set), fewer than 5% critical hallucinations.

Redwood recommendations (shortlist) — tuned for throughput, tail latency, and quality:
1) Redwood-verified small quant (rw-7b-q4f) — best cost/TPS balance for high-throughput inference; good for short-form summarization.
2) Mistral-instruct-13B-8k (quantized profile) — stronger instruction-following quality; expect ~2x cost vs rw-7b but higher factuality on long context.
3) Llama2-70B-causal (optimized kernels, kv-cache) — reserved for high-quality long-form answers where hallucination risk is highest. Use as fallback variant.

Performance snapshots (Redwood-verified) — linked below. Highlights from our lab runs (2x A100 equivalent, 8-token sampling):
- rw-7b-q4f: steady-state TPS 45 req/s, p50 85ms, p95 220ms
- mistral-instruct-13b-8k (q6): TPS 18 req/s, p50 180ms, p95 480ms
- llama2-70b: TPS 3–5 req/s, p50 600ms, p95 1.6s

Quality/Regression guardrails
- We observed instruction slip for very long contexts (>10k tokens) on the smaller models; recommend prefix-conditioning + system prompt templates and a dedicated prompt set for regression checks.
- We’ll include a baseline eval harness (your 800-case set) to run nightly regressions against any model/quantization change.

Pilot proposal (next steps)
- Deliverables: Redwood-verified perf pack + prompt set (attached), pilot pricing sheet, SOC2 & security links.
- Timeline: pilot kick-off w/in 2 business weeks after PO; 3-week pilot: week1 baseline runs + integration; week2 performance tuning; week3 business-case readout.
- Suggested capacity: shared hosted with dedicated burst (start: 2 reserved GPUs equivalent).

Attachments and links
- redwood_verified_profiles_20281129.csv (performance profiles by model/sequence length)
- orion_mvp_promptset_v1.zip (starter prompts + regression harness)
- Drive perf traces: https://drive.redwood.ai/benchmarks/OR-2028-43/perf-traces

Ask / immediate actions
1) Please confirm the pilot capacity budget constraints (we suggested 2 GPUs equivalent).
2) Confirm procurement contact (I see procurement@orion-analytics.com on the thread — thanks).
3) If agreed, we’ll send a short SOW + pilot pricing and a DocuSign link by end of day.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20m sync to walk through the perf pack.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

From: Carmen Diaz <carmen@orion-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Geller <alex@orion-analytics.com>, procurement@orion-analytics.com
Date: Thu, 29 Nov 2028 12:45:30 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap — model recommendations, bench links & pilot next steps

Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the concise recap — this is very helpful. A few clarifying Qs before we finalize the pilot PO: 

- Can you confirm p95 numbers when we sample at our expected 2k response length (you reported lab numbers for 8-token sampling)? We need tail latency under 1.5s for the majority of requests.
- For rw-7b-q4f, what degradation in factuality did you see on the 800-case set vs Mistral? A short metric (e.g., exact-match or factuality score) would help.
- Please attach SOC2 and any FedRAMP-lite or cloud-region constraints; our security team will triage.

I’m looping in procurement (procurement@orion-analytics.com). We’re targeting a week-to-week pilot — open to the 2 GPU suggestion if we can see realistic p95 numbers on our 2k token workload.

Can your team run a quick p95-focused trace for rw-7b-q4f and mistral-instruct-13b on the 2k prompt distribution and share the perf traces?

Thanks,
Carmen
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion Analytics

Carmen — quick update from ops/pricing side.

We’ll run the targeted p95 traces against your 2k-token distribution — Marcus will own the run and share raw traces (S3/Drive) by EOD tomorrow. Note the lab numbers Hannah sent were sampling-light; p95 scales with sampling length and temperature knobs.

Pilot commercial proposal (summary):
- Pilot SKU: Hosted Pilot (reserved capacity) — 2 GPU-equivalents, 3 weeks
- Pilot price (not final): $18,000 flat for the pilot window (includes perf runs, tuning, and 3 readout sessions).
- Add-on: Dedicated capacity ramp pricing if you convert to Reserved (we’ll provide a break-even after pilot).

Attached: pilot_pricing_sheet_OR-2028-43.pdf (pricing + SOW bullet points).

DocuSign & procurement
- Draft SOW/PO link: https://hubspot.com/deal/OR-2028-43 (we’ll drop the DocuSign link into HubSpot once you confirm).

Attachments included in this message: pilot_pricing_sheet_OR-2028-43.pdf

On the security front: Hannah linked the SOC2 report above; if your team needs a secure-upload of the SOC2 package we can send a presigned link or set up an NDA-protected share.

—
